name: Wimberley Market Days
desc: First-Saturday open-air market running March through December. Booth spaces are assigned by seniority, with a rolling waitlist for new vendors. Approval is rolling via email (leasing@wimberleymarketday.com), not a fixed application deadline; booths are typically rented the week before each market day.

name: Fredericksburg Trade Days
desc: Three-day Hill Country market held the third weekend of each month across covered barns and open field lots. Pricing varies by space: $75-$135 for outdoor lots, $150-$273 for indoor barn spaces (10x14 to 15x14). No published application deadline or jury process; contact 210-846-4094 to book.

name: Bayou City Art Festival
desc: Juried fine art festival drawing a national applicant pool across 19 media categories. Panel review with blind scoring. This is the Memorial Park edition (Fri-Sun); booth fees range $525-$1775 by category/size plus a separate $50 non-refundable jury fee. Accepted artists notified by Jul 6. Public admission is $18 early-bird/$20 regular per day (kids 6-12 $5, 5 and under free), or $30 for a weekend pass.

name: Comicpalooza
desc: Multi-genre pop culture convention with a dedicated Artist Alley. Tables sell out in tiers; early registration opens to prior-year vendors. UNVERIFIED: 2027 exhibitor applications aren't open yet (interest form only as of Aug 2026) — no official 2027 dates, pricing, or deadline published. Current start/end/deadline/fee below are unconfirmed placeholders. Public admission ($68 single-day, ~$119 weekend pass) is reference pricing carried over from the completed May 2026 event via secondary media coverage — the official site no longer publishes 2026 prices and hasn't posted 2027 numbers yet.

name: Armadillo Christmas Bazaar
desc: Ten-day juried holiday art market with live music. Long-run format favors vendors with deep inventory and staffing help. Booth fees run ~$1,500-$5,000+ by size (avg ~$2,000) plus a $25 application fee. Applications are accepted year-round on a rolling basis; Jan-Mar submissions get priority, with primary review Mar-Aug. Returning artists get priority over new applicants in popular categories. Public admission is $12 (+fees, ~$14 total) per day, or $60 for a season pass; kids 12 and under free.

name: First Monday Trade Days
desc: One of the largest recurring open-air markets in the country, spanning several hundred acres over four days each month. UNVERIFIED: the grounds are split across many independently-operated pavilions, each with its own booth pricing and contact — there is no single official fee. Call the City of Canton First Monday office at 903-567-6556 for a specific venue's rate.

name: Cottonwood Art Festival
desc: Twice-yearly juried fine art festival in a shaded park setting. Jury reviews three work images plus one booth shot. $500 covers a single booth; a double booth is $1,000 (limited) and electricity is a $100 add-on. A separate $35 non-refundable jury/application fee is paid per entry via ZAPPlication.

name: Blue Genie Art Bazaar
desc: Consignment-model holiday bazaar. No booth fee or staffing requirement; the venue takes a percentage of sales instead. The Yelp "Temporarily Closed" status is normal seasonal downtime, not a shutdown — the storefront is a holiday-only operation that reopens each November for the season (confirmed reopening November 2026), consistent with this listing's window. Public admission is believed free (multiple secondary sources agree; the official FAQ page returned a 404 during verification, so treat as likely rather than confirmed).

name: Anime Matsuri
desc: Anime and Japanese culture convention with a large artist alley and separate dealer hall. Table assignment by registration order. Corrected from a stale March placeholder — Anime Matsuri actually runs in July; the 2026 edition (Jul 23-26) is confirmed and uncancelled, and 2027 is set for Jul 22-25 (per Eventbrite, though organizers note dates may shift). Applications open Sept 8 with price tiers increasing Dec 1/Mar 1/Jun 1 - exact table price not published outside the application form, so the $380 figure and Dec 1 "deadline" (first price-increase date) are best-effort estimates. Public admission tiers are $65 Fri/$70 Sat/$45 Sun from the official badge page, but tied to the just-completed 2026 dates and carried as reference pricing since 2027 isn't priced yet.

name: Main Street Fort Worth Arts Festival
desc: Four-day juried street festival with very high foot traffic. Booths are on pavement; weights required in place of stakes. Standard 10x10 booth is $995 (corner $1,145), plus a separate $40 non-refundable application fee. Roughly 200 artists are jury-selected from nearly 1,000 applicants.

name: Emerald City Comic Con
desc: Artist Alley is curated via portfolio review, not a lottery or first-come order. Accepted artists get a 6' table plus 2 badges for $430, due in full by the January deadline to hold the space. 2027 applications are already closed as of this writing; a waitlist is available. Public admission is $84 Saturday single-day (tax/fees included), $64.05 Fri/Sun, $27.30 Thursday preview — confirmed on the official 2027 ticket page.

name: Round Top Antiques Fair
desc: Roughly two-and-a-half-week destination market spread across 48+ independent show fields (not nine days as previously listed). Early fields like Bar W Field, Henkel Square, and The Marketplace Warrenton open Oct 15; most of the 48+ venues run the official Oct 17-31 window. Space is leased directly from individual field operators (e.g. Zapp Hall, Excess Fields, Marburger Farm, Big Red Barn) - pricing and application process vary by field and remain unconfirmed here; the $900 fee is an unverified placeholder. Public admission is similarly fragmented across the 48+ fields — most are free to browse, but the flagship "Original Round Top Antiques Fair" field charges its own $10 general/$25 VIP admission, so no single admission price applies to the market as a whole.

name: Texas Renaissance Festival
desc: Eight-weekend seasonal festival requiring period-appropriate merchandise and shop presentation. Multi-season vendors get renewal priority. Confirmed: the vendor application itself carries a $50 non-refundable fee. The $1,400 figure here is presumed to be the actual shop/booth lease, but I could not confirm that number from the source PDF (binary-encoded, didn't extract cleanly) — needs a second look. Public admission is NOT free and has no single flat price — the official site confirms dynamic per-weekend pricing from roughly $16-27 (early/off-peak weekends like Oktoberfest) up to $28-46+ (peak weekends like Pirate Adventure, Halloween, Highland Fling), advance vs. gate. The $28 stored here is a typical non-peak gate-day figure, not an official constant.

name: Austin Flea
desc: Recurring indie maker pop-up hosted at rotating bars and venues. Low entry cost makes it a common first market for new vendors. Booths run $50-$75/event (varies by venue, listed per application) plus a $5/yr new-vendor tent/display approval fee. Each application is individually juried; Texas Sales Tax Permit required. Local, handmade/vintage sellers only — no imported goods.

name: Dallas Fan Expo
desc: Large pop culture convention with tiered artist alley pricing by table location and corner access. Corrected from a placeholder May 2027 date - the confirmed, upcoming edition is Sep 11-13, 2026 at the Kay Bailey Hutchison Convention Center (2027 dates aren't announced yet). Standard 6x5 table is $480; premium 5x12 end-cap is $1,060. No fixed application deadline is published - tables sell until they run out, so this date is an estimated planning buffer, not an official cutoff. Public single-day admission is $58 Saturday/$48 Sunday/$33 Friday per the official ticketing partner's live checkout page (base price before service fee) — confirmed as current pricing, though the site notes "advanced pricing" ends Aug 27, 2026 and may step up to a higher tier before the show.

name: Nutcracker Market
desc: Massive juried holiday shopping market fundraising for Houston Ballet, drawing over 100,000 shoppers across a preview party plus four show days at NRG Center. Unlike a flat booth-fee model, Houston Ballet also takes an 11% commission on merchant sales on top of space cost, and charges a separate non-refundable $25 application fee. Exact booth pricing tiers weren't accessible (pricing page blocked automated access), so the $2,500 fee here is a rough placeholder based on comparable high-traffic juried holiday markets, not a confirmed price - confirm real pricing and the application deadline directly before applying. Public admission is $20/day general, or $60 for a 4-day early-bird pass; kids 2 and under free.

name: Denton Arts & Jazz Festival
desc: Long-running juried art show paired with a large free jazz festival, recently relocated to the North Texas Fairgrounds and shifted from its traditional spring slot to Sep 11-13, 2026 (worth double-checking before relying on the old April date elsewhere). 10x10 booths available indoor/outdoor; a $50/exhibitor surcharge applies for shared booths. Jun 1 is the no-surcharge cutoff, not a hard close - late fees of $20 (after Jun 1) and $50 (after Aug 1) suggest applications are still accepted this close to the show, just at a premium; the Aug 20 date here is an estimated last-call, not an official cutoff. Base booth fee was never published anywhere I could find - the $300 here is an unverified estimate, not a confirmed price. Attendance (~200k) is the festival's historical figure from its old Quakertown Park venue and may not hold at the new fairgrounds site.

name: Boerne Market Days
desc: Recurring Hill Country market on Boerne's historic Main Plaza, held the second weekend of every month (plus a bonus December date not reflected in this listing's auto-computed schedule). Vendors reapply each month they want to participate. Booth fees must be paid by the 1st of the month before the show and are non-refundable, but the actual dollar amount isn't published online - the $40 here is a rough estimate based on comparable small-town Hill Country markets, not a confirmed price. Contact davidquerbach@eventsoffmain.com or (210) 844-8193 to confirm current pricing and attendance before applying. Public admission is inferred free — the official page lists public market hours with no fee mentioned, but there's no explicit "free" statement either.

name: Pancakes & Booze Art Show
desc: Traveling one-night "anti-gallery" art show at The Far Out Lounge & Stage — free pancakes, full bar, live body-painting, 75+ local artists showing 300+ pieces. 18+ event. No jury and no commission: accepted artists just pay a flat per-piece wall-hanging fee (the $15 here is a national average figure, not Austin-confirmed — the org states it varies by city). A separate vendor lane exists for craft/product sellers, but no table fee is published. Applications are rolling until the venue fills, so the deadline shown is an estimated planning buffer, not an official cutoff. Public admission is $17 early-bird / $23 day-of (confirmed via Eventbrite). Attendance is a rough estimate based on comparable Pancakes & Booze editions in other cities — no official total is published.

name: Art & Beer Night Market Austin
desc: Annual evening market at The Brewtorium pairing 70+ local artists/makers with craft beer and food. Confirmed to have run in both 2024 (Nov 9) and 2025 (Nov 8) — both landed on the 2nd Saturday of November, which is the pattern this listing's date is computed from, but the 2026 edition hasn't been officially announced yet, so treat the date as inferred, not confirmed. Booth fee, public admission price, and application deadline are all unconfirmed — no organizer page publishes dollar figures; the $75 fee shown is a rough estimate based on comparable small Austin maker markets. Outdoor/brewery-grounds setting is inferred from the venue, not explicitly stated. Watch the organizer's Instagram (@artandbeeraustin) for the official 2026 announcement before applying.

name: Fiesta Arts Fair
org: UT San Antonio (Southwest School of Art)
desc: Nationally-ranked juried fine art & craft fair (Top 50, Art Fair SourceBook) held on UTSA's historic Southwest campus as part of Fiesta San Antonio, drawing 100-120+ artists from ~30 states. The Nov 1, 2026 application deadline is real and actionable — applications for the next edition just opened via ZAPPlication — but the show's own 2027 dates aren't announced yet; the Apr 17-18, 2027 shown here is an estimated placeholder following the fair's usual mid-to-late-April slot. Booth fee ($350+) and jury fee ($26) are stale figures from a 2017-18 secondary source, not confirmed current pricing. Public admission ($16 for a 2-day ticket) is confirmed for the just-completed April 2026 edition. Attendance is a rough midpoint of conflicting secondary estimates (8,000-12,000).

name: Old Gruene Market Days
desc: Long-running monthly artisan market (~100 vendors) in the Gruene Historic District selling handmade crafts and Texas-made packaged foods, with free live entertainment. Runs the 3rd full weekend of the month, February through November, plus a bonus 1st-weekend-of-December date not reflected in this listing's auto-computed schedule (same modeling limitation as Boerne's extra December date — see README). It is juried, so it's not a walk-on market, but no application deadline is published anywhere the organizer's site would confirm (site blocked automated access) — shown as rolling until confirmed; contact the Gruene Merchants Association directly. Booth fee ($60) is an estimate based on comparable small monthly Hill Country markets, not an organizer-published figure. Admission and parking are confirmed free. Attendance (~4,000/weekend) is a secondary-source estimate, not an official organizer figure.

name: Hub City Art & Craft Vendor Market
desc: Small, three-day indie craft/art market for local artists, crafters, and small boutique businesses (jewelry, candles, fine art, woodworking, home decor, specialty foods with approval) at the Municipal Garden & Arts Center. Application is informal — a direct email to the organizer (jeremysanders612@gmail.com) rather than a jury or formal platform — making it a genuinely low-barrier option for new/emerging vendors, though that also means little published pricing data. Booth fee, public admission, and attendance are all unconfirmed estimates based on comparable small local markets; confirm directly with the organizer before applying.

name: Chalk the Block
org: City of El Paso Museums and Cultural Affairs Department
desc: Large, free, city-run public arts festival in Downtown El Paso combining a major chalk-art competition (judged, with a $2,000 "Best of Show" prize) with an artisan/cottage-food vendor market and food trucks — one of the best-attended events in this directory, with attendance confirmed across multiple independent sources. Note: the 2026 artisan-vendor application deadline (Jul 31) has already passed as of this listing's verification date — treat this as a "watch for next year's application window, expect similar October timing" reference rather than a currently-open call. Vendor booth fee is unconfirmed (no dollar figure published); the $150 shown is a rough estimate based on comparable city-run festival vendor fees. Public admission is confirmed free.

name: Dia de los Muertos Arts & Crafts Expo
desc: Juried arts-and-crafts expo ("Hecho a Mano") embedded in Corpus Christi's large annual Dia de los Muertos street festival, now in its 19th year and repeatedly named a top Dia de los Muertos celebration nationally. Single booth (10'x10') is $125, double is $250, plus a separate non-refundable $10 application fee; a mandatory vendor meeting is held before the event. Public admission is confirmed free (a separate ticketed VIP preview party is optional/extra). Overall public attendance isn't published anywhere official — the $8,000 shown is a rough estimate based on the festival's scale (85-100+ vendor booths) and its repeated "best festival" recognition, not a confirmed figure.

name: Art in the Square
desc: Long-running (26+ years) juried fine art festival at Southlake Town Square, run entirely by volunteers of the Southlake Women's Club to benefit Tarrant County charities, drawing 150+ artists and repeatedly ranked #1 by Art Fair SourceBook. Single booth (10'x10') is $550, double is $1,050, and there's a distinctive $300 Emerging Artist tier for developing DFW-area artists — plus a separate $40 non-refundable application fee. Public admission is confirmed free. Attendance is reported as "tens of thousands" across organizer and third-party sources, but no precise official total is published — the 40,000 shown is an order-of-magnitude estimate, not a hard count.

name: Celebration of the Arts
desc: Self-described cornerstone fine art & fine craft event of the Permian Basin, now in its 42nd+ year, held fully indoors (rain-or-shine, air-conditioned) at the Bush Convention Center with 40+ regional/out-of-state artists across painting, fiber, photography, jewelry, wood, and glass, plus cash jury awards. The just-completed 43rd edition's booth fee was never published beyond a $25 non-refundable ZAPPlication application fee — the $450 shown is a rough estimate based on comparably-sized indoor Texas art fairs, not an organizer-confirmed price. 2027 show dates aren't announced yet (next cycle typically opens in December); the May 14-16 window shown is an estimated placeholder following the fair's usual mid-May slot. Saturday/Sunday admission is confirmed free (a separate ticketed Friday preview party is $80-85, not general admission). Attendance is unconfirmed — no official total is published; 5,000 is a conservative estimate for a regional indoor fair of this size.

name: Rose Festival Arts and Crafts Fair
desc: Long-running fair paired with the historic Texas Rose Festival at Bergfeld Park, with 90-100+ booths of handcrafted goods (jewelry, candles, pottery, wreaths, mixed-media art) plus live music and food trucks. Data quality here is thinner than most listings: the City of Tyler's own event pages are currently unreachable (404/site restructure), so the booth fee was never independently confirmed — the $55 shown is an estimate based on comparable small regional craft fairs, not an official figure. Jury status is reported by a secondary source (FestivalNet) but not independently verified on an official page. Confirm current pricing directly with City of Tyler Parks & Rec (~903-531-1214) before applying. Admission is confirmed free; attendance (~3,000) is also a secondary-source estimate, not an official City of Tyler figure.
